title: Plot3D structured grid format
overview: Plot3D is a family of structured-grid conventions used in CFD. Files may contain one or multiple blocks, dimensions and coordinate arrays; variants differ in ASCII/binary encoding, precision, record markers and optional iblank data.
principle: Plot3D stores structured index-space connectivity implicitly. Neighbours are inferred from i-j-k ordering and block dimensions rather than explicit element connectivity. Point count Np=ni*nj*nk; for a non-degenerate 3-D block, Nc=(ni-1)(nj-1)(nk-1). Preserve dimensions, ordering, precision and blanking semantics.
architecture: The current OneFLOW path reads Plot3D through GridMediator and writes CGNS through CgnsFactory::DumpCgnsGrid, preserving the structured block/zone path. Standard Plot3D stores connectivity implicitly through block dimensions and i-j-k ordering. An optional Plot3D-to-CGNS-Unstructured adapter can expand those blocks into ordered QUAD_4 / HEXA_8 cells, populate UnstructuredMeshData and call UnstructuredCgnsZoneWriter. This is a topology transformation, not a native unstructured Plot3D reader; it must preserve IBLANK and block-interface semantics and obtain boundary meaning from explicit source metadata or configuration. This optional route is not implemented yet.

proves: The current Plot3D conversion entry point uses GridMediatorGroup and the structured CGNS writer path.
The contract distinguishes standard Plot3D implicit structured topology from an optional, not-yet-implemented structured-to-unstructured expansion route.
does_not_prove: Every ASCII/binary and record-marker variant is supported or independently verified.
All ASCII/binary, endian, precision and Fortran record variants are supported.
Boundary conditions or interfaces can be inferred from coordinates alone.
